messages:
alex_kaplan: Quick dump from this morning's probe run across sm86/sm92. Ran the sequence-breaker sweep (len thresholds 64/128/512) + quant mix (INT8/INT4/FP8). Posting raw findings and a couple config snippets so we can decide fallback thresholds.

maya_singh: Thanks — can you paste the perf numbers? even rough p50/p95 helps.

alex_kaplan: p50 (tokens/ms): sm86 INT8: 0.012, INT4: 0.010, FP8: 0.011; sm92 INT8: 0.010, INT4: 0.009, FP8: 0.0095. p95 shows more divergence: sm86 INT4 p95 regressed ~18% vs INT8 on long seqs (>512).

cj: hmm that p95 hit on sm86 INT4 — was KV cache warm-up accounted for?

alex_kaplan: yes, tests included cold->warm phases. The regression appears when the KV cache grows past ~1.2M entries; kernel selection flips to an INT4 matmul path that has lower throughput for big KV lookups.

lia_wong: Do we have the kernel pick logs? I want to see the heuristics that chose INT4 for those seq lengths.

alex_kaplan: pasted below — it's the runtime's pick trace for a single request sequence:

```
[2026-03-10T09:12:33Z] model:redwood-1 quant:INT4 arch:sm86 seq:768 tokens
pick: matmul_kernel_v2_int4 (lat_est: 9.3ms)
alt: matmul_kernel_fp8_fast (lat_est: 8.6ms)
reason: batch_estimator -> favors int4 for steady-state small batch
note: kvcache_miss_ratio spike=0.22
fallback delayed by hysteresis=2 runs
```

maya_singh: Wait the alt FP8 path had lower estimated latency — why wasn't it chosen?

alex_kaplan: estimator used median batch size=1.8 in that window; int4 had slightly better per-op perf for small micro-batches historically, so pick stuck. But when KV lookup overheads kick in it changes effective cost.

sriram_nair: This suggests our cost model is missing sequence-length dependent KV overhead. We need an additive term for kvcache ops proportional to (seq_len * kv_miss_ratio).

cj: Agree. Also consider a probe window to sample actual end-to-end latency before committing to int4 path for >256 tokens. If probe shows >10% higher latency, flip to FP8 for next N requests.

lia_wong: Proposed quick config to test:
```
kernel_autotune:
  seq_thresholds: [128, 384, 1024]
  probe_window: 6
  probe_max_extra_tokens: 64
  kv_penalty_weight: 0.8
  fallback_backoff: 3
```

alex_kaplan: Will run that config this afternoon and post results. If it helps, I also have a small trace that demonstrates the warmup cliff — attaching inline:

```
perf-trace: requests 1..120
- warmup 1..8: kvcache cold, latency high
- stable 9..60: int4 chosen, p50 good
- growth 61..90: kvcache size doubled, int4 p95 spikes
- manual flip to fp8 at 91: p95 recovers
```

maya_singh: Nice. Could we also log kernel memory footprints? INT4 path is using a specialized workspace that might thrash L2/L3 on sm86.

alex_kaplan: good call. I'll enable per-kernel med counters in the next run (low overhead mode).

perf-bot: autotune-run 1849012389 completed (config-id: probe-logbook-v1). Summary: saw 12% p95 improvement after probe-window enabled for seq>384 using kv_penalty_weight=0.8. Full logs at /perf/runs/1849012389

cj: sweet. If numbers hold, let's bake probe_window=6 and kv_penalty_weight=0.8 into canary policy for sm86 only, leave sm92 on current heuristic.

sriram_nair: I'll open a PR to adjust the cost-model and add kv_penalty term. Assigning to @alex_kaplan for integration tests.

alex_kaplan: taking it. I'll post run 2 by EOD with kernel mem counters. :thumbsup:
